title: AWS CWI Training in Omaha, NE: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Omaha welders in poles and towers, railcar repair, data centers and bridges: corporate, online or one-to-one sessions.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Omaha, Nebraska: Six Days for Structural, Rail and Construction Welding Inspectors
html:
Most of what Omaha welds is steel that carries a load: transmission and lighting poles, wireless towers, center pivot irrigation machines, railcars, data center frames and the girders of bridges over the Missouri and Platte. Many of the people who check that work hold the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential or are working toward it. Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for the CWI examination in a six-day (6-day) course that takes in all three parts, Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. Omaha candidates choose between corporate delivery at their employer's facility, online study at their own pace, and six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor. AWS administers the examination and is the body that certifies inspectors; the course prepares people and certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Omaha. Atlantis works from offices in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India, and reaches Nebraska and western Iowa through the three formats below. Ask for a price through the Omaha CWI enquiry form.

Three ways to take the six days from Omaha

The six-day outline does not change with the format. Two days of fundamentals cover processes, terminology, joint design, welding symbols, metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities, NDT methods, fabrication math, safety and the inspector's responsibilities. The third day prepares for the practical, the fourth works through your chosen code book, the fifth is timed practice exams, and the sixth closes gaps and covers exam-day logistics. The AWS CWI exam prep page sets out each day in detail.

Corporate delivery for an Omaha employer

A pole and tower plant, a railcar repair shop, a structural fabricator or a contractor's quality group can have all six days delivered at its own site for a group of staff, using its gauges, its production welds and, where it fits, its code and procedures.

Online study for an individual

Working alone, you get a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and an instructor answers your questions as you go. No class meets at a set hour; you choose the pace, which matters in a market where construction overtime peaks in summer and outages come without much warning.

One-to-one with the instructor

A single candidate can book six days of one-to-one sessions, held online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It suits an experienced welder who needs intensive help with code navigation, or someone heading back for a part they did not pass.

Whichever format you choose, every practice question is an original written by Atlantis to the subject areas AWS publishes. Nothing is lifted from an AWS examination, and AWS has neither approved nor endorsed the course.

What Omaha welds, sector by sector

Poles, towers and irrigation

Valmont Industries is headquartered in Omaha. Its infrastructure business makes steel and composite structures for electrical transmission, substations and distribution, poles for lighting and transportation, and wireless towers, and it provides galvanizing and coating services; its agriculture business sells center pivot and linear irrigation equipment under the Valley brand. Production welding of tapered poles, base plates, arms and tower sections is high-volume work in which weld size, profile, fit-up and complete fusion are checked constantly, and galvanizing adds its own demands for clean, fully sealed or properly vented welds. AWS D1.1 is the natural Part C book for structures like these.

Construction and engineering

Kiewit, founded in Omaha in 1884 and still headquartered in the city, runs construction and engineering work across North America in power, industrial, transportation and other markets. Contractors of that size staff quality teams on project sites far from Nebraska, and the welding side of a QA/QC team frequently includes CWIs. For Omaha inspectors, that means project assignments that can take them anywhere.

Railcars and locomotives

Union Pacific is headquartered in Omaha, and the city sits on both Union Pacific and BNSF main lines. Railcar repair is local work as well. Greenbrier's Omaha maintenance center on South 28th Street, with access to both railroads, repairs and refurbishes railcars, including wreck repair, with certified welders and nondestructive testing on site, and it cites the Association of American Railroads' M-1003 quality assurance and M-1002 tank car requirements. AWS D15.1, the railroad welding specification for cars and locomotives, is the Part C book written for that world.

Data centers south of the city

Sarpy County has become a data center market. Meta built a campus near Highway 50, and Google broke ground on its first Nebraska data center in Sarpy County in 2019, later buying land northwest of Omaha in Douglas County as well. Buildings like these combine steel frames, heavy support steel for mechanical and electrical equipment, cooling-water piping and standby power, which keeps structural welders and D1.1 inspectors busy between other projects.

Power stations and outages

Within driving distance, OPPD's Nebraska City station and NPPD's Cooper Nuclear Station near Brownville hold maintenance outages that bring in welders, pipefitters and quality staff. Power piping is welded to ASME B31.1 with Section IX procedures, and nuclear work adds the owner's own quality program on top of the code.

Bridges over the Missouri and Platte

River crossings, interstate interchanges and county bridges across Nebraska and western Iowa put steel girder fabrication and repair under AWS D1.5, the bridge welding code. D1.5 includes a fracture control plan for nonredundant members, so bridge shops expect their inspectors to know how its stricter requirements change preheat, filler metal control and testing.

Who asks for a CWI in Omaha

  • Pole, tower and structural manufacturers. In-process inspection, final visual acceptance and welder qualification audits on high-volume lines.
  • Railcar and locomotive repair shops. Inspectors who understand D15.1 and the railroads' quality requirements for repairs and modifications.
  • General contractors and EPC firms. QA/QC staff for power, industrial and infrastructure projects, often away from home for long stretches.
  • Structural fabricators and erectors. D1.1 inspection on data centers, warehouses, hospitals and office buildings, frequently alongside the building code's special inspection.
  • Utilities and outage contractors. Welding QC during planned outages at coal, gas and nuclear stations.
  • Bridge fabricators. Shops supplying state transportation departments need inspectors comfortable with D1.5.

A posting that asks for "CWI, D1.1" and one that asks for "CWI with D15.1" are describing different careers. The book you choose for Part C should match the one you want next.

Part C for Omaha: D1.1, D15.1 or another book?

Part C is open book on a code of your choice. The AWS list includes D1.1 (structural steel), API 1104 (pipelines), D1.2 (aluminum), D1.5 (bridges), D15.1 (railcars and locomotives), D17.1 (aerospace fusion welding), an ASME package of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Here is how Omaha work maps onto them.

Work in front of youCode bookTypical Part C ground
Poles, towers, irrigation structures, data center and building steelAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, procedure and welder qualification, tolerances and visual acceptance
Railcar and locomotive repair and modificationAWS D15.1Qualification and workmanship requirements written for cars and locomotives
Bridge girders and repairs for state and county ownersAWS D1.5Bridge qualification rules, the fracture control plan and acceptance for tension members
Power station piping and outage workASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Essential variables, qualified ranges, and piping examination and acceptance
Gas transmission and pipeline repairAPI 1104Destructive-test qualification and acceptance standards for pipeline welds

Use the edition AWS names for your exam, which may be older than the copy in your shop. Background reading: AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and the WPS, PQR and WPQ guide.

The AWS Nebraska Section

The AWS Nebraska Section, part of District 16, has held its recent events in Omaha and nearby towns. In 2026 its program included a tour of Rebellion Fabrication in Wahoo; an evening at Metropolitan Community College's South Omaha campus where a presenter from Nippon Sanso-Matheson spoke about welding procedure specifications and district and section awards were handed out; the section's 32nd annual golf outing; a student welding conference at Southeast Community College, co-hosted with the Southeast Nebraska Section, with a Fronius technology demonstration; and an industry tour at Patriot Millwright Services. A talk on procedure specifications is useful CWI preparation in its own right, because checking work against a WPS and its qualification record runs through Parts B and C. Section members are also the people most likely to confirm your welding experience when AWS asks.

Metropolitan Community College and Omaha's welding pipeline

Metropolitan Community College offers an Associate in Applied Science in Welding Technology at its South Omaha campus. The program trains students in the major welding processes, standard construction and industry procedures and safety, and finishes with a fabrication project read from welding blueprints. Its catalog lists stick and gas-shielded pipe welding courses and welder qualification courses, so graduates leave with qualifications they can carry from job to job. Southeast Community College trains welders to the south, and many Nebraska manufacturers train their own people on the production line.

An associate degree in a field AWS accepts can bring the CWI experience requirement down to two years, compared with five for a high school diploma alone. AWS makes that call on each application, so send transcripts with it, and keep your welder qualification records, which help prove the welding-related history AWS asks you to document.

Booking the CWI exam from Omaha

AWS sends a confirmation with an eligibility code once it accepts your application. With that code you book the two computer-based parts, Fundamentals and Code Application, through Prometric, which AWS says has more than 100 centers in the United States. The practical is booked with AWS and happens only at its seminar and examination locations on dates AWS sets, so a session in another state is a real possibility for Nebraska candidates. Check the AWS schedule early and plan time off around it.

What you will face: Part A is 150 multiple-choice questions; Part B is hands-on work with AWS-supplied tools and specimens plus 46 questions; Part C is roughly 50 to 65 questions with the code book open. AWS sets the minimum at 72 percent per part. AWS lists its examination fees on aws.org. The course itself is quoted on request, and the CWI exam cost planner covers the other items worth budgeting. For published figures on how candidates fare by part, see CWI results by part.

Studying around construction seasons and outages

Nebraska's year has a shape. Outdoor construction and erection work peaks in the warmer months and slows in deep winter, plant outages tend to fall in spring and fall when power demand is lower, and production plants run steady shifts with overtime when orders climb. Online study lets you take advantage of whichever lull comes first. A practical rhythm: work through symbols, processes and metallurgy during the quieter months, carry your code book to the shop and look up the clauses that govern the welds you are checking, measure real welds with your own fillet and bridge cam gauges, and keep the timed papers for the final stretch before your Prometric appointment. Send questions to the instructor as they arise rather than saving them up.

Corporate delivery at an Omaha plant, shop or yard

For an employer preparing several people, the six days can be delivered at the company's own facility. A pole plant can run the practical exercises on its own production welds and base-plate connections; a railcar shop can spend the code day in D15.1; a contractor with mixed crews can split the code day between D1.1 and the ASME book. Dates can be fitted around production peaks, outage schedules and the construction season. Every candidate still files an individual application with AWS and meets the experience and vision requirements personally; that part cannot be handled by the employer.

One-to-one sessions, online or in person

The one-to-one format is six days of sessions between one candidate and the instructor, run online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Because the pace is yours alone, the six days can be weighted heavily toward your weakest area, whether that is fabrication math, reading welding symbols at speed or finding clauses in an unfamiliar book. A QC supervisor whose company needs one qualified inspector before a contract begins is a typical one-to-one candidate.

Eligibility and the vision test

The experience AWS asks for depends on your education: five years of welding-related work with a high school diploma, one year with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, two with a qualifying associate degree, four after completed trade or vocational courses, and longer with less schooling. AWS needs experience it can verify on welded products, such as fabrication, construction, inspection or repair. Separately, you must submit an AWS Visual Acuity Record showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without correction, plus a color perception test, carried out by a qualified professional within the period AWS allows before your exam. Full details are on the AWS CWI course page and in the CWI requirements guide. If you do not yet have enough years, the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) lets you inspect under the direction of a CWI while you build them.

After the CWI in Omaha

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewal paperwork at the third and sixth years and recertification at the ninth. Omaha inspectors move on in several directions: into quality management at a manufacturer, onto national project work with a large contractor, into the railcar side with D15.1, or toward the AWS Senior CWI for those who end up running inspection programs (see the Senior CWI pathway). Many add nondestructive testing so they can perform the ultrasonic, magnetic particle or penetrant tests that structural and rail customers ask for. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A an employer certifies its NDT technicians after training and documented experience, and Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A-based training: see NDT training in Omaha, MT Level 2 training, ultrasonic testing in Omaha and nuclear NDT training for the Omaha area. To see how the CWI compares with other credentials, read CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II.

Nearby pages and an Omaha quote

Other CWI exam prep pages in the region: Kansas City, Minneapolis, Denver and Wichita. For the method side of weld quality, see weld inspection and Practical NDT for Omaha.

For a quote, let us know the format you want (corporate, online or one-to-one), how many people want to prepare, each person's education and welding work in outline, and the Part C book each expects to choose. For delivery at your site, add the location, the gauges and sample welds you can supply, and the weeks to avoid because of production or outages. Use the Omaha CWI enquiry form.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Omaha for the CWI course?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Omaha. You can take the six-day course as corporate delivery at your employer's facility, as online study at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, or as six days of one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking. See the outline.

faq.q: Who certifies a welding inspector as a CWI?
faq.a: The American Welding Society. AWS administers the examination, checks your eligibility and issues the CWI. Atlantis prepares candidates for that examination and certifies no one.

faq.q: Which Part C book suits pole, tower and structural work in Omaha?
faq.a: AWS D1.1, the structural welding code for steel. It covers the prequalified joints, qualification rules and visual acceptance criteria that structural and pole fabrication depends on. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: I inspect railcar repairs. Should I take D15.1 for Part C?
faq.a: If railcar or locomotive work is where you want to stay, yes. AWS D15.1 is the railroad welding specification for cars and locomotives and is one of the Part C options AWS offers.

faq.q: Where do Omaha candidates take the CWI exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are booked with Prometric using the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation. Part B is held only at AWS seminar and examination locations on dates AWS sets, which may mean travelling to another state.

faq.q: Can a pole plant or fabrication shop host the six days?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery takes place at your facility, uses your gauges and production welds, and can follow D1.1 or another code your group works to. Request a quote.

faq.q: Are one-to-one sessions available online as well as in person?
faq.a: Yes. The six days of one-to-one sessions can run online or in person at a location agreed when booking, and the time is weighted toward the topics you find hardest.

faq.q: Does a Metropolitan Community College welding degree help with eligibility?
faq.a: An associate degree in a field AWS accepts can reduce the experience requirement to two years, against five with a high school diploma. AWS decides on each application, so include transcripts.

faq.q: Do the practice questions come from the AWS exam?
faq.a: No. They are original questions written by Atlantis to the published AWS subject areas, and Atlantis has no access to the live examination.
